name: The Thelemic Pantheon
dom: Thelema; the deities of Liber AL; the new aeon
note: The collective of deities and praeterhuman intelligences central to Aleister Crowley's Thelema as set out in Liber AL vel Legis (1904) and its surrounding corpus.

name: Hoor-paar-kraat
note: The silent passive twin of Ra-Hoor-Khuit, the god of silence; a Thelemic adaptation of Harpocrates forming a polarity with the active conquering child.

name: Babalon
dom: the Great Mother; ecstasy; the Scarlet Woman; liberation; the Abyss
note: The Thelemic Great Mother and sacred-whore goddess riding the Beast, developed by Crowley (notably in The Vision and the Voice) as a redemptive reframing of the biblical Whore of Babylon.

name: Therion (The Beast 666)
dom: force; the magical self; prophecy; consort of Babalon
note: To Mega Therion, 'The Great Beast 666,' Crowley's prophetic magical office and consort of Babalon; an affirmative reclamation of the apocalyptic Beast of Revelation.

name: Choronzon
dom: the Abyss; dispersion; chaos; dissolution of the ego
note: The demon and 'dweller in the Abyss' encountered in the 10th Aethyr; first named in John Dee's Enochian records and greatly developed by Crowley into the Thelemic embodiment of dispersion.

name: The Holy Guardian Angel
dom: the true self; tutelary spirit; attainment; knowledge and conversation
note: The Thelemic/Abramelin concept of the individual's tutelary genius or true higher self, whose 'Knowledge and Conversation' is the central attainment; adopted from the Book of Abramelin and recast by Crowley, who identified Aiwass as his own HGA.

name: The Aeon of Horus
dom: the present age; the crowned and conquering child; self-realization
note: The current cosmic age inaugurated in 1904 according to Thelema, succeeding the Aeons of Isis and Osiris and governed by Ra-Hoor-Khuit; modeled as an era rather than a being.

name: The Theosophical Spiritual Hierarchy
dom: the spiritual hierarchy of beings governing planetary and cosmic evolution
note: The graded hierarchy of spiritual beings — the Masters, the Lord of the World, the Logoi, and the Lords of Karma — said in Theosophy to oversee human and planetary evolution.

name: Morya (Master M.)
dom: hidden wisdom; spiritual guidance; the first ray of will
note: Master Morya, one of the Mahatmas said to stand behind the Theosophical Society and to have corresponded with Blavatsky; a being original to the modern Theosophical movement.

name: Koot Hoomi (Master K.H.)
dom: hidden wisdom; spiritual guidance; the second ray of love-wisdom
note: Master Koot Hoomi (Kuthumi), one of the principal Mahatmas of Theosophy and chief author of the Mahatma Letters; a being original to the modern Theosophical movement.

name: Djwal Khul (The Tibetan)
note: Master Djwal Khul, 'the Tibetan,' a Mahatma later said to have telepathically dictated the books written through Alice Bailey; a being of the modern Theosophical tradition.

name: The Maha Chohan
dom: hidden wisdom; spiritual administration; the third ray
note: The 'Great Lord,' chief of the third ray and head of the Masters' hierarchy of civilization in Theosophical teaching; a being original to the modern Theosophical movement.

name: Sanat Kumara
dom: the Lord of the World; Shamballa; planetary governance; the Ancient of Days
note: The 'Lord of the World' and 'Ancient of Days' said to dwell at Shamballa and govern Earth's spiritual evolution; a Theosophical adaptation of the Hindu Kumara name into a modern cosmic office.

name: The Solar Logos
dom: the solar system; cosmic consciousness; the divine animating logos
note: The Theosophical conception of the divine intelligence ensouling and governing the entire solar system, developed within the modern revival from the Greek philosophical Logos.

name: The Planetary Logos
dom: planetary governance; the Earth-chain; cosmic consciousness
note: The Theosophical divine intelligence ensouling a single planet, subordinate to the Solar Logos; a modern-revival cosmological office.

name: The Lords of Karma (The Lipika)
dom: karma; the cosmic record; the law of cause and effect; the akashic record
note: The Lipika, the 'recorders' or Lords of Karma described in Blavatsky's The Secret Doctrine who register every act and administer the law of karma; a collective being of modern Theosophical cosmology.

name: The Root Races
dom: human evolution; cosmic cycles; the seven humanities
note: The series of seven successive cosmological humanities (Lemurian, Atlantean, Aryan, ...) through which spirit evolves in The Secret Doctrine; modeled as a single collective rather than seven entities.

name: The Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
dom: ceremonial magic; initiation; the Western esoteric synthesis
note: The influential English initiatory magical order founded in 1888 that synthesized Qabalah, Enochian, Egyptian, and Tarot systems; a synthesizing framework rather than a source of new beings.

name: The Secret Chiefs
dom: hidden authority; initiation; direction of the Order
note: The hidden Third-Order adepts said to direct the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn through its leaders (notably claimed by Mathers); a concept paralleling and influenced by the Theosophical Masters.
